blocks.explanation:
Parametric equations hain, aur saabit karna hai ke second derivative \(-2\) hai.
Diya kya hai? \(x = \sin t\), \(y = \cos^{2}t\).
Saabit kya karna hai? \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 2 = 0\).
Rule kaunsa? \(y_{1} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\), aur \(y_{2} = \frac{d}{dt}(y_{1})\cdot\frac{dt}{dx}\).
Plan: \(t\) wale derivatives, \(y_{1}\), phir \(y_{2}\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x = \sin t\), \(y = \cos^{2}t\).
Saabit karna: \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 2 = 0\).
Tareeqa: parametric differentiation do dafa.

\(t\) ke lehaz se derivatives
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \cos t\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 2\cos t(-\sin t) = -2\sin t\cos t\]
Kyun: \(\cos^{2}t = (\cos t)^{2}\), to power rule aur chain rule: \(2\cos t\) times \(\cos t\) ka derivative \(-\sin t\).
Dhyan dein: \(\cos^{2}t\) ka derivative \(-\sin^{2}t\) likhna ghalat hai.

Pehla derivative
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-2\sin t\cos t}{\cos t} = -2\sin t\]
Kyun: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\); \(\cos t \ne 0\) maan kar cancel kiya.

Doosra derivative
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(-2\sin t)\cdot\dfrac{dt}{dx}\]
\[= -2\cos t\cdot\dfrac{1}{\cos t} = -2\]
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 2 = 0\]
Kyun: \(-2\sin t\) ka \(t\) wala derivative \(-2\cos t\), aur \(\frac{dt}{dx} = \frac{1}{dx/dt} = \frac{1}{\cos t}\). \(\cos t\) cancel ho kar \(-2\) bacha.

Tasdeeq
\(t\) ko khatam kar ke dekhiye: \(y = \cos^{2}t = 1 - \sin^{2}t = 1 - x^{2}\). Yeh parabola hai, jis ka \(y_{1} = -2x\) aur \(y_{2} = -2\). Seedha wohi jawab mil gaya.
